notes: Stored ABox edit for relation-property coverage (ABox inheritance and role chain). The edit moves an individual work from one class to another (novel to epic poem). Inheritance: every epic poem is written in verse, so the story is told in verse (no to yes). Chain: instance_of carries chain:subclass_of->instance_of, and epic poem is a subclass of narrative poem, so the work is a narrative poem (no to yes). Both class links are firm (an epic is by definition a long narrative poem in verse), so both queries are determinate. Derivability very_unlikely: the form is stated in the article's first sentence (207 exact 'epic high fantasy novel'). Background beliefs (verifier, round 2): the writer's split through the volumes was dropped. Its w1 needed The Two Towers and The Return of the King to stop being volumes of The Lord of the Rings, which contradicts firm facts outside the chain (the 1954-55 three-volume publication under those titles, the films 'The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers' and '...: The Return of the King'); with w1 gone both volume queries were determinate. The split is now the dolphin pattern (biology-replace-0013): the work's structure is stored about it by name (w1: chapters, the first 'A Long-expected Party', 577 exact hits for the title in two cases) or reached through its form (w2: an epic poem is divided into books or cantos and opens with an invocation to a muse, a convention in the textbook lists of epic characteristics). Neither world contradicts a firm fact: an epic poem may keep chapters and its own opening (w1), and the edit already rewrites the text in verse, so a new opening breaks nothing outside it (w2). w1 is likely the majority world; lopsided worlds are kept (Decisions 4). R1: the original 'no' to 'told in verse' refers to the narrative, which is prose; the book contains songs and poems ('Lord of the Rings AND verse' 4,451), which is why the prompts ask about the story. The work has 62 chapters and no invocation (0 'Lord of the Rings AND invocation to the Muse'). Near query (author) is untouched by the edit. Avoided 'Is it a work of fiction?': fantasy already entails fiction, so it would not discriminate.
